A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same quantization and LLM-unlearning study. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments, SURE evaluations, hyperparameter analysis, and ablations on NEWS, BOOKS, and RWKU, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds BOOKS results for RMU and RMU_LAT in Appendix I, Table 11.

M1.justification: SURE's module-level gradient saliency mask, thresholding, and large-learning-rate updates remain unchanged in Section 6.1. RMU and RMU_LAT are additional evaluated methods, not revisions to SURE.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NEWS, BOOKS, RWKU, and the same general-utility tasks. The new RMU experiments use existing BOOKS coverage. Appendix F's description of RWKU's 200 selected individuals clarifies the retained benchmark rather than establishing new coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix I adds evaluated RMU and RMU_LAT comparisons before and after quantization, while retaining the earlier comparison methods. LAT is evaluated through its combination with RMU; Task Vector and the attacks discussed in Appendix L are not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new RMU/RMU_LAT experiments introduce a learning-rate search over 5e-6, 1e-5, and 5e-5. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 newly documents backbone preparation rather than reporting a revision to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix I extends quantization robustness testing to methods intended to encourage deeper forgetting in model representations, finding recovery for both RMU and RMU_LAT. The existing saliency ablation in Table 10 and threshold analysis in Table 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. Table 11 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results. New Table 11 reports RMU's verbatim memorization increasing from 14.2 to 50.5 after quantization and RMU_LAT's from 11.7 to 43.0; knowledge memorization increases from 0.0 to 29.3 and 27.4, respectively. These are added results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, quantization-interval reasoning, and SURE equations remain unchanged. Appendix J discusses the existing theoretical explanation without adding or correcting a derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: quantization can recover forgotten knowledge, small weight changes explain the phenomenon, and SURE can mitigate it. The new title does not establish a different scientific claim.

C2.justification: Appendices I–J newly acknowledge potentially less-vulnerable non-finetuning methods and describe SURE as an initial, nonexclusive mitigation. Appendices K–L expand deployment and legal-risk implications and contrast quantization with extraction attacks. The original mechanism and utility-tradeoff interpretations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.3 identifies the LLaMA-2 7B and ICLM-7B backbones, model provenance, data-exclusion rationale, and five-epoch preparation at learning rate 1e-5. Appendix F adds RWKU data-selection details, Appendix I supplies its learning-rate grid, and Appendix M adds an anonymous code location while the original public link remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine references supporting targeted discussion of RMU/LAT, task-vector methods, robust-unlearning evaluations, low-bit quantization, and backbone models. Appendix L newly positions quantization relative to prior extraction attacks, while the main related-work sections remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled 'Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization,' gains conference headers, Appendix C.3, and Appendices I–M, and receives small wording corrections. The existing narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11, uses blue highlighting for selected appendix additions, and reflows existing table floats and Figure 2's placement. The retained figures and Tables 1–10 preserve their substantive display structure.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.3 improves reproducibility by identifying previously unspecified backbones and their preparation, while Table 11 extends the failure evidence beyond the original method families. These are useful, bounded gains. Both new methods have zero full-precision retain-set utility, limiting conclusions about utility-preserving unlearning, and Appendix L claims superiority over prior attacks without a matched comparison. The central method, theory, and existing results remain unchanged.
